typical_symptoms: Angular, water-soaked spots on leaves bounded by minor veins
Reddish-brown to black necrotic lesions on leaf blades and veins
Dark, water-soaked sunken lesions on cotton bolls
Blackened, elongated girdling lesions on stems and petioles (black arm stage)
Premature defoliation and leaf drop under high humidity
visual_characteristics: Small geometric spots confined by leaf veinlets
Greasy or water-soaked appearance on leaf undersides
Necrotic centers surrounded by dark red or purple borders
Dark vein necrosis extending outward from infection points
lesion_characteristics: Angular, multi-sided shapes restricted strictly by leaf micro-veins
Sharp, well-defined margins with a thin reddish-purple border
Sunken, dark brown to black necrotic center
Individual spots typically 1 to 5 mm in diameter
color_characteristics: Initially translucent or water-soaked dull green
Turns dark reddish-brown, dark maroon, or black with age
Yellowish chlorotic halo occasionally surrounding older lesions
texture_characteristics: Dry, papery, and brittle in mature necrotic tissue
spatial_patterns: Scattered individual angular spots across the interveinal leaf tissue
Vein-associated linear streaks following primary and secondary leaf veins
Coalescing spots forming large, irregular necrotic blighted patches
distinguishing_features: Strictly angular geometry enforced by leaf veinlets
Water-soaked appearance on the abaxial (lower) leaf surface
Involvement of petioles and stems causing characteristic 'black arm' lesions
commonly_confused_with: Nutritional leaf reddening or deficiency symptoms
